newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's INSEE sees unemployment edging higher.
newsitem.headline: France's INSEE sees unemployment edging higher.

text.p: French unemployment, already at a record 12.7 percent, is likely to continue climbing to reach 12.9 percent in June, national statistics institute INSEE said in an economic outlook published on Tuesday.
In an otherwise upbeat assessment of economic prospects, it said economic growth would accelerate in the second half of the year, helped by the rise in the dollar.
"The impetus provided by foreign demand and by the fall in interest rates looks like being sufficiently strong and lasting to draw domestic demand progressively along in its wake," it said.
It left unchanged however a forecast made in December that gross domestic product growth would be an average 0.9 percent in the first half of this year. It made no forecast for the second half.
The government is forecasting growth of at least 2.3 percent over the full year, after a rise of 1.3 percent last year.
INSEE said an acceleration in growth could happen even earlier if expectations of rising prices encouraged faster-than-expected stockbuilding.
A rise of 10 percent in the dollar would add 0.4 percent to French gross domestic product growth, with the main impact seen in the second half of the year.
In its last forecasts in December, INSEE assumed a dollar exchange rate of 5.10 francs, whereas it is now trading around 5.70 francs.

Unemployment remained one of the black spots in the overall forecasts. INSEE had in December forecast unemployment would reach 13 percent in June, a figure some economists had said was overly pessimistic.
INSEE however described the downward revision of its jobless rate forecast to 12.9 percent in June as "fragile", and was unable to say whether unemployment would peak at this level.
"Unemployment is going to be the angry buzzword in France through the (parliamentary) elections next March," Smith Barney economist Paul Horne told Reuters Financial Television.
Morgan Stanley economist Eric Chaney however contested the forecasts, saying he saw an improvement in employment.
"I think unemployment will fall in France as soon as March or April," he said.

"I do not think unemployment will peak at 13 percent in June, and what is funny is that the official forecasts and the government are more gloomy than (French) consumers who have understood that the labour market is improving in France," he added.
